scope_note: cs.CV/cs.RO /new listing for 2026-07-29 was parsed with the repository scripts. The parser found 104 non-replacement cs.CV rows and 41 non-replacement cs.RO rows; after deduplication, 140 papers remained and 117 were classified as ROI. Tier A uses official arXiv HTML full text for CoTinyVLA, HiFi-UMI, IDR, SAM3D-VLA, DC-WAM, FIRMGrasp, SONG, and track-leakage-free photogrammetric validation.
executive_thesis: The July 29 batch makes the same research decision appear in three different places: robot policies, simulators, and geometric validators are being forced to expose the evidence that justifies an action before the final success score is trusted. CoTinyVLA compresses a VLA by distilling phase-level reasoning rather than simply shrinking a backbone. HiFi-UMI asks whether robot-free data can become deployable once pose, synchronization, and field-of-view fidelity are tight enough. IDR, SAM3D-VLA, and DC-WAM each move hidden modality choice, object-centric 3D priors, or dynamic visual evidence into the action path. FIRMGrasp and the photogrammetry protocol show the same move in validation: nominal confidence is not enough unless the adverse tail or leakage path is explicit. SONG turns social navigation from a policy leaderboard into a photorealistic, safety-aware episode generator. APRL should treat these as a mandate to build evidence-bearing rollout logs: reasoning span, data-source fidelity, causal modality effect, 3D object prior, dynamic token, friction risk margin, social-safety state, and geometry self-validation should be recorded before model size is compared.

decision_cards.label: Decision
decision_cards.title: Small robot policies need structured evidence, not just distillation loss
decision_cards.body: CoTinyVLA's useful move is that the teacher distills phase, gripper state, and next subaction. The student is smaller, but the important artifact is the reasoning contract that can be audited per failure.

decision_cards.label: Decision
decision_cards.title: Robot-free data is only a substitute when fidelity is typed
decision_cards.body: HiFi-UMI does not argue that any human demonstration can replace robot data. It narrows the claim to microsecond synchronization, accurate relative pose, wide hand views, and replay validation.

decision_cards.label: Decision
decision_cards.title: Validation metrics must name the blind spot they cannot see
decision_cards.body: FIRMGrasp discounts adverse friction tails and the photogrammetry protocol separates internal consistency from absolute accuracy. Both are valuable because they state what the metric does not certify.

papers.title: CoTinyVLA: Chain-of-Thought Distillation for a Sub-Billion-Parameter Vision-Language-Action Model
papers.fit: compact VLA - chain-of-thought distillation - LIBERO-Plus robustness
papers.status: Tier A - official arXiv HTML verified
papers.status_quo: Robotics papers often treat VLA robustness as a backbone scale problem, leaving the smaller model to imitate actions without a visible task-phase rationale.
papers.friction: Embedded robots need low memory use, but compact action models usually lose robustness on initial-state, object, and long-horizon perturbations.
papers.hidden_premise: A small VLA can inherit useful structure if the teacher exposes an episode plan and chunk-level reasoning, rather than only final actions.
papers.conceptual_move: CoTinyVLA distills hierarchical reasoning into a 0.9B VLA with dual-view temporal history and paraphrase-expanded language supervision.
papers.mechanism: The model assembles third-person frames, wrist frames, proprioception, and instruction tokens, then distills Plan and Think spans from a larger teacher into action prediction.

evidence.claim: The architecture is organized as a four-stage pipeline with dual camera histories, proprioception, language, hierarchical CoT, and action prediction.
The paper defines hierarchical chain-of-thought supervision with episode-level Plan and chunk-level Think spans.
LIBERO-Plus Spatial and Object tables report higher total success than the strongest 7B baseline.
Closed-loop inference peaks at 2.25 GiB allocated GPU memory, and removing or contradicting the episode Plan costs 40 to 45 success points.

papers.falsification: If Plan/Think spans improve only prompt paraphrase robustness but not physical perturbations, the method is mostly language regularization.
papers.adversarial: Teacher reasoning can be plausible but wrong. The release needs failure cases where the distilled Plan is inspected against actual robot state transitions.
papers.thinking_tool: Log a robot action together with the compact model's phase explanation, gripper-state belief, and next subaction, then score which field fails first.
papers.transfer_boundary: The idea transfers to manipulation tasks with stable subtask phases. It is weaker for highly reactive contact tasks where language-level phase is not the limiting variable.

papers.title: HiFi-UMI: Learning Deployable Manipulation Policies from High-Fidelity UMI Data Alone
papers.fit: UMI data - deployable manipulation - synchronization and pose fidelity
papers.status: Tier A - official arXiv HTML verified
papers.status_quo: Robot-free demonstrations are usually treated as scalable pretraining data, while a smaller real-robot anchor is still assumed necessary for deployment.
papers.friction: UMI data can scale, but inaccurate hand pose, poor synchronization, and narrow field of view can make the learned policy brittle on the robot.
papers.hidden_premise: A robot-free corpus can replace a real-robot anchor only when the capture system preserves the control-relevant state at deployment fidelity.
papers.conceptual_move: HiFi-UMI co-designs head-mounted stereo-inertial SLAM, native relative pose, microsecond GPIO synchronization, and wide hand cameras for high-fidelity robot-free data.
papers.mechanism: The device and processing pipeline reconstruct high-quality hand trajectories and validate demonstrations through simulation replay before using them for policy post-training.

evidence.claim: The paper presents a robot-free pipeline from data collection through real-robot policy deployment.
The capture device combines a head-mounted stereo camera pair, per-hand marker cubes, and synchronized wide-angle hand cameras.
Data-quality criteria are a first-class part of the system rather than an afterthought.
The paper reports 3 mm workspace-local end-effector accuracy and direct deployment without robot post-training across three policy backbones.

papers.falsification: If zero-robot post-training fails outside the captured scene family, the system may still be an in-domain teleoperation substitute rather than a general data moat.
papers.adversarial: Fidelity can be concentrated in pose while contact force, compliance, or object dynamics remain missing. Replay validation should expose which failure modes the corpus cannot see.
papers.thinking_tool: Evaluate data sources by the state variables they preserve: relative pose, synchronization, hand-object visibility, replay pass rate, and contact ambiguity.
papers.transfer_boundary: The claim transfers to visuomotor manipulation with visible gripper-object geometry; force-dominated tasks still need additional sensing or real-robot labels.

papers.title: A Causality-aware Infer-diagnose-refine Framework for Test-time Modality Adaptation in VLA Models
papers.fit: VLA test-time adaptation - causal visual importance - frozen policy refinement
papers.status: Tier A - official arXiv HTML verified
papers.status_quo: VLA models usually fuse vision, language, and proprioception with a fixed learned balance, even though task phases change which modality should matter.
papers.friction: Close-range interaction and long-distance motion can require different visual reliance, but retraining for every phase or camera condition is impractical.
papers.hidden_premise: The policy can diagnose visual importance by comparing factual and counterfactual action predictions at test time.
papers.conceptual_move: IDR keeps the VLA frozen, intervenes on visual observations, estimates causal effects, and uses them to refine the action in a training-free way.
papers.mechanism: Zero-padding interventions create counterfactual actions; norm-based causal effects estimate dynamic visual importance; gated residual fusion refines the base action.

evidence.claim: The paper contrasts direct multimodal fusion with IDR's factual and counterfactual action paths.
IDR is a frozen-model test-time wrapper with infer, diagnose, and refine stages.
The causal graph frames visual intervention as the basis for modality-effect estimation.
The method defines the infer-diagnose-refine framework as the core algorithmic loop.

papers.falsification: If counterfactual visual padding changes action magnitude for nuisance reasons rather than causal task relevance, the diagnostic signal can be misleading.
papers.adversarial: A frozen VLA may already encode spurious visual shortcuts; IDR can refine them rather than remove them unless the intervention family is stress-tested.
papers.thinking_tool: For each action step, store factual action, visual-counterfactual action, causal-effect norm, and refined action to locate phase-specific modality failure.
papers.transfer_boundary: The wrapper transfers to existing VLA backbones; it depends on an intervention that isolates the modality without destroying unrelated task context.

papers.title: SAM3D-Guided Object-Centric Representation Alignment for Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.fit: object-centric 3D supervision - VLA alignment - long-horizon manipulation
papers.status: Tier A - official arXiv HTML verified
papers.status_quo: Many VLA policies inherit 2D visual-language backbones and hope that object pose, scale, and occlusion robustness emerge from RGB-language training.
papers.friction: Manipulation often fails at the target-object relation, especially when subtasks shift attention across objects and views.
papers.hidden_premise: 3D object priors can be injected during training while preserving the original RGB-language-to-action test-time pipeline.
papers.conceptual_move: The paper uses SAM3D as a frozen teacher to align object-centric 3D representations with intermediate VLA visual features.
papers.mechanism: Task instructions are decomposed into subtasks, relevant object masks are generated, SAM3D extracts dense object-level 3D features, and the VLA aligns to those features during training.

evidence.claim: The method is presented as an object-centric 3D alignment framework using SAM3D as frozen training-time teacher.
Task-relevant masks feed the SAM3D teacher and supervise intermediate VLA features.
The paper compares the method with state-of-the-art approaches on the LIBERO benchmark.
The paper includes limitations, which is important because SAM3D supervision is still teacher-dependent.

papers.falsification: If gains disappear under objects outside SAM3D's reliable geometry prior, the alignment may be teacher-specific rather than a general 3D reasoning capability.
papers.adversarial: The test-time policy does not receive depth, masks, or SAM3D. A distribution shift that breaks learned object priors can fail silently.
papers.thinking_tool: Treat frozen 3D teachers as training-time sensors and measure which object-relation failures they actually remove from the rollout log.
papers.transfer_boundary: The idea transfers to object-centric manipulation; deformable objects, fluids, and tool use need a different teacher or explicit runtime sensing.

papers.title: DC-WAM: Dynamic-Centric Visual Supervision and Reasoning for World-Action Models
papers.fit: world-action model - dynamic visual tokens - control-relevant foresight
papers.status: Tier A - official arXiv HTML verified
papers.status_quo: World-action models often optimize future-image fidelity, which can spend capacity on texture and lighting that do not determine the next action.
papers.friction: The video branch is expensive, and it is unclear whether photorealistic prediction or control-relevant dynamics are responsible for policy gains.
papers.hidden_premise: The visual branch should preserve interaction-induced changes, not reconstruct every appearance detail.
papers.conceptual_move: DC-WAM redirects RGB future supervision toward dynamic regions and uses DynaRoute attention bias to emphasize control-relevant future tokens.
papers.mechanism: Temporal-difference flow matching, trajectory-guided weighting, and token-wise dynamic relevance bias the model toward gripper, object, and contact-area changes.

evidence.claim: The paper reports lower PSNR with higher policy success, arguing against appearance fidelity as the decisive objective.
The architecture combines dynamic-centric dense and sparse supervision with attention routing.
Under perturbations, DC-WAM keeps attention closer to dynamic regions while the baseline shifts toward distractors.
The method makes dynamic supervision part of the optimization, not a post-hoc interpretation.

papers.falsification: If dynamic routing helps only the benchmark scenes used to create tracker-derived maps, the method may be overfitting supervision artifacts.
papers.adversarial: Motion is not always task relevance; moving distractors and stationary task-critical objects can reverse the assumption.
papers.thinking_tool: For WAM policies, log which future tokens were kept or emphasized, then test whether those tokens predict action success better than PSNR.
papers.transfer_boundary: The method transfers to tasks where contact or object motion carries the decision. It needs safeguards for static constraints and moving distractors.

papers.title: FIRMGrasp: A Friction-Informed Risk Margin for Robust Grasp Synthesis
papers.fit: risk-aware grasp metric - friction uncertainty - CVaR margin
papers.status: Tier A - official arXiv HTML verified
papers.status_quo: Classical grasp scores often assume one friction coefficient, so a grasp can look high-quality while failing under the adverse part of the friction distribution.
papers.friction: Dexterous grasp deployment depends on uncertain contact surfaces, not just nominal force closure.
papers.hidden_premise: The metric should evaluate the adverse friction tail directly and expose a probabilistic closure certificate.
papers.conceptual_move: FIRMGrasp defines a CVaR-discounted friction-informed margin for the risk-adjusted grasp wrench space.
papers.mechanism: The method replaces a single nominal friction value with a risk-adjusted friction term and evaluates the inscribed-ball radius of the corresponding wrench space.

evidence.claim: The paper shows nominally similar Allegro grasps that separate under adverse friction risk.
The risk-adjusted margin is constructed from a friction prior and adverse-tail discounting.
Risk-sensitive grasp quality is the central method section.
Across 1,599 LEAP Hand and Allegro grasps, 53% certified by the nominal margin lose force closure in the adverse friction tail.

papers.falsification: If calibrated friction distributions are unavailable or unstable, the risk margin can be mathematically clean but operationally underdetermined.
papers.adversarial: CVaR over friction does not cover geometry error, tactile slip detection, or object compliance. The certificate is not a full grasp-success guarantee.
papers.thinking_tool: Replace single-score grasp selection with an adverse-tail margin and log which assumed uncertainty distribution made the grasp acceptable.
papers.transfer_boundary: This transfers to grasp synthesis with friction priors; it needs coupling with perception and tactile feedback for real object handling.

papers.title: SONG: A Photorealistic 3D Gaussian Simulation Platform for Benchmarking Social Navigation
papers.fit: 3DGS simulation - social navigation - safety and compliance benchmark
papers.status: Tier A - official arXiv HTML verified
papers.status_quo: Social navigation benchmarks often simplify pedestrians, rendering, or observations enough that vision-based policies avoid the hardest deployment evidence.
papers.friction: A robot must navigate from onboard visual observations while moving people create both safety and social-compliance constraints.
papers.hidden_premise: A useful social-navigation benchmark needs photorealistic scene appearance, dynamic human avatars, and metrics beyond task success.
papers.conceptual_move: SONG builds a 3D Gaussian simulation platform with photorealistic environments, dynamic avatars, semantic episode synthesis, and a multidimensional metric suite.
papers.mechanism: 3D Gaussian scenes and avatars are prepared as assets; LLM-generated semantic trajectories and motion generation produce social episodes for closed-loop agents.

evidence.claim: The overview presents 1,000 photorealistic 3DGS environments and 500 dynamic human avatars.
The pipeline covers asset preparation, semantic episode synthesis, and dynamic Gaussian rendering.
SONG is compared with social-navigation platforms on representation, animation, and observation fidelity.
The benchmark defines an evaluation protocol rather than only a simulator implementation.

papers.falsification: If policies trained in SONG do not transfer across real social layouts and crowd dynamics, photorealistic rendering may not be the missing variable.
papers.adversarial: LLM-generated pedestrian trajectories can encode plausible but non-human behavior. Social compliance metrics need real-world behavioral calibration.
papers.thinking_tool: Design navigation benchmarks as episode generators with separate effectiveness, safety, and compliance labels.
papers.transfer_boundary: The platform helps vision-based navigation and social compliance; it is less direct for contact-rich manipulation or non-human dynamic obstacles.

papers.title: Track-Leakage-Free Hold-Out Self-Validation for Photogrammetric Reconstruction: Protocol, Sensitivity, and Limits
papers.fit: photogrammetric validation - leakage-free hold-out - internal consistency limit
papers.status: Tier A - official arXiv HTML verified
papers.status_quo: Reconstruction pipelines often want a no-ground-truth confidence score, but hold-out views can leak structure or mistake internal consistency for absolute accuracy.
papers.friction: A robot or inspection system can have a self-consistent map that is globally wrong, and a high confidence score can hide that failure.
papers.hidden_premise: Self-validation is useful only when the protocol states exactly which leakage path it blocks and which error family it cannot certify.
papers.conceptual_move: The paper withholds images and re-localizes them only against 3D points seen by retained images, creating a track-level barrier.
papers.mechanism: A deterministic hold-out subset is evaluated by resection against trusted tracks and aggregated into an mAA-style confidence score.

evidence.claim: The protocol relocalizes held-out views against retained-view structure and excludes points the view helped create.
The paper illustrates both the track-level leakage barrier and the blind spot to self-consistent global distortion.
The re-BA ablation compares the paper's hold-out test with an independent bundle-adjustment variant.
The results separate leakage control and hold-out fraction sensitivity from absolute accuracy certification.

papers.falsification: If the protocol is used as a deployment accuracy gate, the paper's own blind-spot analysis invalidates that use.
papers.adversarial: Internal consistency metrics can reward a coherent wrong world. Robot mapping needs external anchors or downstream task checks.
papers.thinking_tool: Every self-validation metric should publish a blocked-leakage list and a known-blind-spot list before being accepted as a gate.
papers.transfer_boundary: The protocol transfers to reconstruction QA and map self-checking; it cannot replace ground truth, control points, or robot task validation.

synthesis.title: S1 - Robot policies are being judged by exposed intermediate evidence
synthesis.facts: The papers expose reasoning spans, causal modality effects, object-centric 3D priors, and dynamic visual tokens inside the action path.
synthesis.inference: The shared research decision is where to make the policy's hidden state inspectable before the action is executed.
synthesis.decision: APRL should log phase reasoning, visual-causal effect, 3D object prior, and dynamic-token salience for each manipulation rollout.

synthesis.title: S2 - Data scale is now a fidelity-and-replay question
synthesis.facts: One paper makes robot-free manipulation data deployable by tightening capture fidelity; the other builds photorealistic social-navigation episodes with safety and compliance metrics.
synthesis.inference: More data matters only when the collection system names the physical state it preserves and the failure family it can replay.
synthesis.decision: APRL should attach a fidelity ledger and replay-validation result to every new data source before mixing it into policy training.

synthesis.title: S3 - Robustness metrics are useful only when their adverse case is explicit
synthesis.facts: FIRMGrasp evaluates adverse friction tails; the photogrammetry paper blocks track leakage while warning that global distortion can remain invisible.
synthesis.inference: A metric becomes trustworthy when it states both the tail it measures and the blind spot it leaves uncovered.
synthesis.decision: APRL should publish adverse-tail and blind-spot fields for grasp, mapping, and navigation benchmarks.

frontier_memory.title: The July VLA thread keeps moving toward action-state contracts
frontier_memory.history: Recent releases emphasized tactile tokens, stale-observation correction, and physical guidance for robot actions.
frontier_memory.read: July 29 adds reasoning distillation, causal modality diagnosis, object-centric 3D priors, and dynamic-token routing as inspectable control evidence.

frontier_memory.title: Robot-free data is becoming a measurement problem
frontier_memory.history: Earlier data discussions focused on scale, source mix, and resettable evaluation cells.
frontier_memory.read: HiFi-UMI shifts the question to whether synchronization, pose, field of view, and replay validation are enough to remove a robot anchor.

frontier_memory.title: Photorealistic simulation is being tied to social-safety labels
frontier_memory.history: 3DGS and simulation papers have often optimized rendering fidelity or scene assets.
frontier_memory.read: SONG makes social episode generation, safety deficit, and real-world fine-tuning the point of the simulator.

frontier_memory.title: Most VLA gains still lack per-failure evidence fields
frontier_memory.history: Many papers report aggregate success under perturbations.
frontier_memory.read: The missing artifact is a rollout schema that says which reasoning span, 3D object prior, modality effect, or dynamic token caused recovery or failure.

strategy.title: Evidence-Bearing VLA Rollout Ledger
strategy.thesis: Record the policy's exposed intermediate evidence at every action step: phase plan, causal visual effect, object-centric 3D prior, dynamic-token map, and final action.
strategy.one_week: Instrument two LIBERO-style and one real tabletop task with Plan/Think text, visual-counterfactual action delta, target-object 3D prior flag, and dynamic-token salience.
strategy.four_week: Compare a compact VLA, frozen-model IDR wrapper, 3D-teacher-aligned VLA, and dynamic-centric WAM on the same failure-labeled rollout ledger.
strategy.metric: At least one logged evidence field predicts failure two steps earlier than success/fail labels with AUC >= 0.75.
strategy.stop: If evidence fields are not more predictive than task ID and previous success history, narrow the work to one failure family before scaling.

strategy.title: High-Fidelity Data Source and Replay Ledger
strategy.thesis: Before adding a demonstration source, record which physical variables it preserves and which replay checks certify deployment relevance.
strategy.one_week: Audit current APRL manipulation data for pose accuracy, synchronization, hand-object visibility, replay availability, and known contact blind spots.
strategy.four_week: Build a small HiFi-UMI-style capture and replay validation path for one precision manipulation task, then test whether robot-free post-training removes a real-robot anchor.
strategy.metric: Replay validation predicts real-robot success within 10 percentage points on held-out task variants.
strategy.stop: If synchronization and pose fidelity are not the limiting failures, redirect toward force/tactile labeling instead of more UMI data.

strategy.title: Adverse-Tail Metric Audit
strategy.thesis: Every robotics metric should publish the adverse case it measures and the blind spot it cannot certify.
strategy.one_week: For one grasp metric and one reconstruction confidence metric, write the adverse-tail variable, blocked leakage path, and known blind spot in a benchmark card.
strategy.four_week: Run FIRMGrasp-style friction-tail tests and track-leakage-free reconstruction self-validation on APRL data, then compare metric confidence against downstream failure.
strategy.metric: Benchmark cards prevent at least one false certification case that the nominal score accepts.
strategy.stop: If the adverse-tail card does not change model or grasp selection, keep it as documentation rather than a new benchmark line.
